issues.body: The public method documentation says that a depth of 0 projects the focus itself as a reference, but write_term handles Term::Literal before checking depth >= max_depth. Consequently, JsonProjection::new().with_max_depth(0).project() emits a literal value object for a literal focus rather than an @ref object. This makes the public contract inaccurate and leaves the boundary behavior untested.
issues.fix_hint: Either clarify the documentation that the depth bound applies only to expandable non-literal nodes (the more natural contract, since literals have no outgoing recursion), or move the depth check ahead of literal handling if literal references are genuinely intended. Add a test for a literal focus with max_depth(0) that pins the chosen behavior.
issues.title: with_max_depth(0) does not reference a literal focus as documented

verdict.summary: The projection logic is cycle-safe, deterministic for the represented graph, preserves literal metadata, and is covered by meaningful public-surface tests. One public API contract is nevertheless false for literal focuses: the documented depth-zero behavior is bypassed for literals. The feature test could not be executed in this checkout because the Rust toolchain is unavailable, so this verdict is based on diff-scoped inspection.
